identity.name: Democratic People's Republic of Korea
native_names: 朝鮮民主主義人民共和國

land.text: Korea north of the 38th parallel under the Soviet Civil Administration (infobox: 'Soviet administration north of the 38th parallel: 3 October 1945'; 'Soviet general Terentii Shtykov recommended the establishment of the Soviet Civil Administration in October 1945')

predecessors.note: The Soviet zone had been Japanese Korea until 1945 (empire-of-japan dossier, 1945 loss). Cliopatria starts the DPRK row in 1948.

capitals.name: Pyongyang
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Pyongyang'. UN forces held the city from 19 October to early December 1950 (Korean War page); the page names no wartime seat of government.

rulers.name: Kim Il Sung
rulers.title: leader (premier, later president)
rulers.note: 'Kim Il Sung became premier' with the founding of the DPRK in 1948; 'died of a heart attack in 1994'. The page does not print his titles year by year.

rulers.name: Kim Jong Il
rulers.title: leader
rulers.note: Succeeded his father in 1994; 'On 17 December 2011, Kim Jong Il died from a heart attack.'

rulers.name: Kim Jong Un

keyframe_review.note: 129,479 km2 for 1948-1952: the land north of the 38th parallel (Soviet Civil Administration from 1945; DPRK 'established in the North on 10 July 1948'). The infobox gives 120,538 km2 (today), ratio 1.07, within the grid's precision. The shape stays on the 38th parallel through the war; the Korean War moves of 1950-1951 are ledger occupation events. The page prints 10 July 1948 as the founding date in both infobox and text; a reviewer should check it against other sources. Founding month: 9 September 1948 (Division of Korea page; the North Korea page's 10 July 1948 is the People's Assembly vote).

126,815 km2 for 1953-2023, 2.7 thousand km2 less than 1948-52. The Korean War infobox: 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea', 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong', 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho'. Cliopatria's diff is 29 cells lost (Gangwon, Gyeonggi, Kangwon-do) and 13 gained (Hwanghae), net about 4,000 km2: it agrees. The North Korea infobox gives 120,538 km2 (ratio 1.05).
Same outline as 1953-2023 (126,815 km2); the page gives 120,538 km2 and says the borders with China and Russia lie 'at the Yalu (Amnok) and Tumen rivers'.

ledger.note: 1948: the Democratic People's Republic of Korea is proclaimed in the North. Division of Korea page: 'the establishment of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea in northern Korea on 9 September 1948', after the People's Assembly 'voted to do so on 10 July' and the legislative elections of 25 August. The North Korea and Korean War pages print 'established ... on 10 July 1948', the date of the Assembly vote; the proclamation of 9 September 1948 is used (reviewer jk-02-d). Kim Il Sung became premier; the Soviet Civil Administration had governed the zone since October 1945.

region.text: South Korea except 'a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan' (the Pusan Perimeter), taken by the KPA between 25 June and September 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the Korean People's Army invades the South and holds all but a corner around Pusan. 'On 25 June 1950, North Korea's Korean People's Army (KPA) launched an invasion of South Korea'; 'Seoul was captured by the KPA on 28 June'; 'By September, UN forces were hemmed into a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan.' The radius around Busan is my reading of the corner.

region.text: South Korea except 'a corner of southeast Korea, near Pusan' (the Pusan Perimeter), taken by the KPA between 25 June and September 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the Inchon landing breaks the North Korean hold on the South. 'On 15 September, UN forces landed at Inchon near Seoul, cutting off KPA troops and supply lines'; 'On 25 September, Seoul was recaptured by UN forces.' The page does not say when the last of the South was cleared, so the month is the recapture of Seoul.

region.text: North Korea, entered by UN and ROK forces in October 1950 and given up in December 1950

ledger.note: 1950: UN and ROK forces cross the 38th parallel and take Pyongyang. 'By 1 October, the UNC had driven the KPA past the 38th parallel'; 'The US Eighth Army drove up western Korea and captured Pyongyang on 19 October'; UN forces advanced 'towards the Yalu River (border with China)'. The page does not say how much of the North was held, so the whole shape is the reading.

region.text: North Korea, entered by UN and ROK forces in October 1950 and given up in December 1950

ledger.note: 1950: the Chinese offensives drive the UN forces out of North Korea. 'UN forces retreated from North Korea in December, following the PVA's first and second offensive'; 'In early December UN forces... evacuated Pyongyang along with refugees.'

region.text: Seoul, captured by the PVA and KPA on 4 January 1951 and lost to a UN counter-offensive two months later

ledger.note: 1951: the Chinese and North Korean armies take Seoul a second time. 'The offensive overwhelmed UN forces, allowing the PVA and KPA to capture Seoul for the second time on 4 January 1951.' The page gives no front line beyond the capital, so the zone is a radius around Seoul.

region.text: Seoul, captured by the PVA and KPA on 4 January 1951 and lost to a UN counter-offensive two months later

ledger.note: 1951: the UN counter-offensive retakes Seoul. 'Communist forces captured Seoul again in January 1951 before losing it to a UN counter-offensive two months later'; 'UN forces retook territory roughly up to the 38th parallel.' March is the page's two months after January.

region.text: the front line of the war of attrition, along what became the Korean Demilitarized Zone

ledger.note: 1951: truce talks begin and the front hardens along what becomes the DMZ. 'Armistice negotiations began in July 1951, but dragged on as the fighting became a war of attrition.' The page gives no front-line positions for 1951-1953, so the zone is a band along the 1953 line (page silent).

region.text: the front line of the war of attrition, along what became the Korean Demilitarized Zone

ledger.note: 1953: the Korean Armistice Agreement ends the fighting. 'Combat ended on 27 July 1953 with the signing of the Korean Armistice Agreement'; it 'created a 4-kilometre wide (2.5 mile) Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) along the frontline'.

region.text: the land south of the front that South Korea gained in the east (Sokcho, Gangwon) in 1953, net 3,900 km2 from North Korea; 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho'

ledger.note: 1953: the armistice line gives South Korea a strip in the east. Infobox: 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea'; 'South Korea gains the city of Sokcho'. Cliopatria's 1953 shapes agree: North Korea loses 29 cells (Gangwon, Gyeonggi) and gains 13 in Hwanghae (about 4,000 km2 net).

region.text: the land in Hwanghae, with Kaesong, that North Korea gained in 1953; 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong'

ledger.note: 1953: North Korea gains Kaesong at the armistice. Infobox territorial changes: 'North Korea gains the city of Kaesong'; the strip of Hwanghae around it comes with it.

wars.outcome: 'Inconclusive'; the Korean Armistice Agreement of 27 July 1953 created the Korean Demilitarized Zone along the front; 'A net total of 3,900 km2 changes hand from North Korea to South Korea', North Korea gaining Kaesong and South Korea Sokcho.
wars.note: Front by year: 1950 June-September the KPA holds the South down to the Pusan corner; 15 September Inchon landing; October-December UN forces hold Pyongyang and push towards the Yalu (the Chinese enter on 19 October); January-March 1951 the PVA and KPA hold Seoul; spring 1951 the UN line is 'roughly up to the 38th parallel'; July 1951 to July 1953 a war of attrition. The page gives no positions of the front for 1951-1953; the contest zone is a band on the 1953 line. The belligerent list follows the infobox: South Korea and the UN, led by the United States, against North Korea with China and the Soviet Union.

certainty.note: The 38th parallel, the dividing line chosen in 1945, is the southern frontier; the Yalu and Tumen rivers the northern.
The front line moved across the peninsula (June 1950 to March 1951) and then hardened; no positions for 1951-1952 are on the pages opened.
The armistice of 27 July 1953 created a 4-kilometre Demilitarized Zone 'along the frontline'; the Yalu (Amnok) and Tumen rivers 'border China and Russia to the north'. The sea frontier is a coast.

notes: Wikidata: Cliopatria's two Korean rows share Q423 (the id of North Korea). They are different states (a northern and a southern government, two Wikipedia articles, two Seshat ids), so no merge: this dossier is the DPRK, the Republic of Korea is a separate dossier. Founding date: the North Korea page prints 'established in the North on 10 July 1948' in both infobox and text; the identity and the found event use it. A reviewer should compare it with the Korean War page or another source (the page may be wrong). The Korean War is carried as occupation events (the KPA in the South from June to September 1950, the UN and ROK in the North from October to December 1950, the PVA and KPA at Seoul in January-March 1951), a contest band along the 1953 line from July 1951, and the 1953 gains and losses; the Republic of Korea dossier has the same events with the roles reversed. The pages do not give the front line for 1951-1953; the Pusan corner, the extent of the UN advance in the North (the whole shape) and the Seoul radius are my readings. Before 1948: the Soviet Civil Administration of October 1945 (infobox) and the Japanese rule before it (the empire-of-japan dossier loses the zone to the USSR in 1945) have no dossier of their own in Korea; the USSR owner is the union-of-soviet-socialist-republics dossier (eu-17). Not on the pages: the 1962 border treaty with China (the page does not mention it), the Russian frontier on the Tumen, the Northern Limit Line and the island disputes, the North's wartime seat of government. The Korean Armistice Agreement page was not opened (budget: two pages). Dokdo/Liancourt Rocks is in South Korea's dossier note.
